correctness.rationale: Idempotents are forced floor maps by monotonicity, regressiveness and fixed-point closure. A gap containing exclusive fixed points of both types yields an explicit evaluation point where compositions differ; otherwise both compositions collapse that gap to its left common fixed point. Each prescribed fiber is an independent product of three-symbol gap assignments, counted exactly as \(2^{\ell+1}-1\). Formal power series produce rank coefficients without convergence issues; independent exhaustive map tests for \(n\le10\) and all Catalan maps for \(n\le8\) agree.

value.rationale: Commuting idempotents and their products are intrinsic structural data of an important finite J-trivial monoid family. The theorem classifies every commuting pair by fixed-point compatibility and gives a multiplicative count for every prescribed product, including equal-rank products with different fiber sizes (7 versus 9 at n=4). This is stronger than a known table: the existing OEIS A206306 records only aggregate rank counts, not compatibility or individual multiplication fibers.
